title: TrustLeak Finding (v2)
description: Breaking change from v1: the single top-level 'confidence' field is replaced by 'relationship.category' plus 'assessment.{evidence_confidence, potential_impact, validation_status}' — separating 'how sure are we this evidence applies' from 'how bad would this be if exploited'. See trustleak-schema-v2-design.md for the full rationale. No v1 compatibility shim is provided by design (schema_version rejects cleanly instead of silently misreading a missing field).

type.description: New types added here must also be registered in trustleak/categories.py's TYPE_TO_CATEGORY — schema.py cross-checks the two and rejects a mismatch (see design doc, open question 4, Option C).

category.description: Groups relationship types by risk mechanism, independent of which analyzer produced them. Only categories at least one current analyzer actually emits are listed here. The HTML analyzer's iframe/script references deliberately reuse framing_dependency/execution_dependency rather than introducing a separate 'embedding' category, since the underlying risk mechanism is identical to their CSP counterparts (see categories.py). navigation_dependency was added for <form action>, a genuinely different mechanism (phishing/credential harvesting, not execution or framing). authentication_dependency covers a passive redirect_uri/AssertionConsumerServiceURL reference found in page text (intercepting a login flow if the dangling subdomain is where the identity provider would send the result) — a future ACTIVE OAuth/SAML discovery analyzer (fetching /.well-known/openid-configuration or SAML metadata) would likely reuse this same category rather than needing a new one. js_content_dependency is the first ACTIVE-probe category (see NOTES.md): a suspicious target's hostname found inside a downloaded .js file's own content, assumed high-impact by default since without executing the script there's no way to tell whether it's an execution-style or data-exfiltration-style reference.

status.description: 'confirmed' is deliberately not a value here — reserved for a human-reviewed pentest finding, never an automated correlation.

evidence_confidence.description: How sure we are this evidence is real and applies to this exact target — driven by whether the policy/header is enforced vs. unenforced (e.g. CSP-Report-Only), whether the matched reference is specific vs. a broad apex wildcard, and ShadowSaaS's own confidence in the target. NOT driven by the kind of relationship — see potential_impact for that.

potential_impact.description: If the takeover happened and this relationship held, how bad would it be — driven purely by relationship.category (see categories.py's CATEGORY_DEFAULT_IMPACT), with a per-finding override for categories that have one (cross_origin_trust escalates with CORS credentials; shared_scope escalates for a session-like cookie name). Does NOT change based on how certain the evidence is.

validation_status.description: Always 'not_validated' today — no analyzer performs active validation yet. Reserved for a future active-probe feature to mark a finding as actively confirmed or ruled out.
